content: 1. Adults are encouraged to receive vaccinations to protect against preventable diseases. The reasons for adult vaccination are explained in detail, emphasizing the importance of staying up to date with immunizations. 2. Information is provided on where adults can access vaccines within their communities, including specialized vaccines for travel purposes. 3. Guidance is available on how to locate personal vaccine records, document vaccinations, and what steps to take if vaccine records are missing or unavailable. 4. Details are outlined on how to pay for vaccines, including options for private insurance, Medicare, Medicaid, and military benefits. 5. Adults are recommended to receive routine vaccinations, and tools like the Adult Vaccine Assessment Tool are available to help determine which vaccines are needed. 6. Staying up to date with COVID-19 vaccinations is emphasized, as it significantly reduces the risk of severe illness. 7. Resources are provided to address questions about preventing seasonal influenza, including the importance of annual flu vaccination. 8. Tetanus vaccination is recommended for individuals of all ages to prevent this potentially life-threatening condition. 9. Vaccination against diphtheria is advised for people of all ages to protect against this serious bacterial infection. 10. The CDC recommends vaccination against whooping cough (pertussis) for individuals of all ages to prevent this highly contagious respiratory disease. 11. Educational resources are available for viewing, downloading, or printing to help individuals learn more about vaccinations and specific vaccines. 12. The CDC provides information on vaccines for travelers, ensuring they are protected against diseases that may be prevalent in their travel destinations. 13. The Standards for Adult Immunization Practice highlight the essential role of healthcare professionals in ensuring adults receive recommended vaccines. 14. Strategies are outlined to improve adult vaccination rates and reduce missed opportunities for immunization. 15. The Partnering for Vaccine Equity (P4VE) Program offers information on promoting equitable access to vaccines across diverse populations. 16. Resources are available to help healthcare providers understand insurance coverage and payment options for vaccines. 17. Communication tools and educational materials are provided for healthcare providers to use or share with patients regarding vaccination. 18. A dedicated resource page is available for healthcare providers on maternal vaccinations, offering guidance on immunizations during pregnancy to protect both mothers and their infants.
